title: 1951 AHSME Problem 10

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: Of the following statements, the one that is incorrect is:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: Doubling the base of a given rectangle doubles the area.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: Doubling the altitude of a triangle doubles the area.

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
Doubling the radius of a given circle doubles
the area.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
Doubling the divisor of a fraction and dividing its numerator
by \(2\) changes the quotient.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
Doubling a given quantity may make it less than it originally
was.

solutions.text:
A circle has area \(\pi r^2.\) Replacing \(r\) by \(2r\) gives \(\pi(2r)^2=4\pi r^2,\) so doubling the radius quadruples, rather than doubles, the area. The other statements can hold as written.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Check how each area formula changes when one length is doubled
A circle’s area depends on the square of its radius
